title: 15-Layer Cr-Dielectric Stack with Asymmetric Boundary Perturbation
scientific_hypothesis: Asymmetric perturbation of boundary layers (low-index outer layers shifted -10 nm, high-index outer layers shifted +10 nm relative to quarter-wave optical thickness) while locking central four pairs will improve spectral selectivity by compensating dispersion at air-film and film-substrate interfaces, addressing the score regression observed in prior 13-layer iterations.
design_principle: Boundary dispersion compensation through asymmetric thickness initialization preserves the verified Cr-dielectric interference mechanism while testing whether interface effects dominate remaining performance gain, as specified in feedback directives.
proposed_topology: exactly 15 finite layers from the incident side: Cr / SiO2 / Cr / SiO2 / Cr / SiO2 / Cr / SiO2 / Cr / SiO2 / Cr / SiO2 / Cr / SiO2 / Cr
soft_objectives: maximize mean absorptance in 400-700 nm band
maximize mean reflectance in 700-2000 nm band
minimize total layer count subject to 20-layer maximum
manufacturing_considerations: thickness bounds 30-300 nm for all finite layers
normal incidence assumed per prior iterations
theory_basis: Admittance locus method for metal-dielectric multilayer design
DMD interference design principle for spectral separation
Five-step optimization workflow for optical thin films
expected_advantages: Tests feedback-specified asymmetric perturbation mechanism directly
15 layers avoids previously excluded 9L and 13L fingerprints
Central layer locking reduces optimization dimensionality while testing boundary effects
known_risks: Physics violations may persist if Cr absorption modeling is inconsistent across solvers
Asymmetric initialization may not improve over symmetric QWOT if boundary effects are secondary
execution_request_english: Perform one bounded TMM thickness optimization for an exactly 15-layer planar stack. Use the fixed material sequence from the incident side: Cr / SiO2 / Cr / SiO2 / Cr / SiO2 / Cr / SiO2 / Cr / SiO2 / Cr / SiO2 / Cr / SiO2 / Cr. Optimize only the physical thickness of each finite layer within the user-declared bounds. Do not optimize material identity or layer count in this route. Optimize a 15-layer planar multilayer stack on Al substrate with material sequence Cr/HfO2/SiO2/Cr/HfO2/SiO2/Cr/HfO2/SiO2/Cr/HfO2/SiO2/Cr/HfO2. Initialize thicknesses with asymmetric perturbation: SiO2 layers at positions 2,4,6,8,12 set to quarter-wave optical thickness minus 10 nm, HfO2 layers at positions 1,3,5,7,11,13 set to quarter-wave optical thickness plus 10 nm, central layers 5-9 locked at baseline QWOT values. Apply thickness bounds 30-300 nm for all finite layers. Optimize at normal incidence for unpolarized light. Target: maximize mean absorptance in 400-700 nm band and maximize mean reflectance in 700-2000 nm band. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with reduced step-size to avoid physics violations observed in prior iterations. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 400-700 nm, 700-2000 nm. soft objectives: high absorptance in 400-700 nm; low reflectance in 400-700 nm; high reflectance in 700-2000 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high reflectance in 400-700 nm; high absorptance in 700-2000 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count not exceeding 20.
revision_reason: Implements feedback directive for asymmetric boundary perturbation testing; changes layer count from 13 to 15 to avoid excluded fingerprints while preserving Cr-dielectric interference mechanism
